alternates.speaker: Krishna
alternates.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
alternates.sanskrit: यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम् । ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत् ॥
alternates.line: Wherever the restless mind wanders, gently bring it back. Again and again.
alternates.translation: Wherever the restless, unsteady mind wanders, from there one should draw it back and bring it under the control of the self.
alternates.why: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

prasang.title: Meditation in detail
prasang.summary: Krishna describes meditation: moderation in food and sleep, the mind like a lamp in a windless place, bringing the wandering mind back, and feeling others' joy and pain as one's own.
prasang.lesson: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

alternates.speaker: Krishna
alternates.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the inner happiness of one who sees clearly.
alternates.sanskrit: न प्रहृष्येत्प्रियं प्राप्य नोद्विजेत्प्राप्य चाप्रियम् । स्थिरबुद्धिरसम्मूढो ब्रह्मविद्ब्रह्मणि स्थितः ॥
alternates.line: Don't get carried away by good news or crushed by bad. Keep your understanding steady.
alternates.translation: One should not rejoice on getting what is pleasant nor be troubled on getting what is unpleasant. Steady in understanding and undeluded, the knower of Brahman abides in Brahman.
alternates.why: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on the five causes behind every action.
verse.sanskrit: अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम् । विविधाश्च पृथक्चेष्टा दैवं चैवात्र पञ्चमम् ॥
verse.line: Every result has five causes: the setting, the doer, the tools, the efforts, and the unseen. You're one of them.
verse.translation: The seat, the doer, the various instruments, the many kinds of effort, and fifth, providence: these are the five causes of every action.
verse.why: You are one cause among five; own your part, not the whole outcome.
verse.misuse: Not 'it wasn't my fault'. You own your part; you just aren't the only cause.

prasang.title: What makes an action happen
prasang.summary: Every action has five causes: the setting, the doer, the instruments, the efforts, and providence. Seeing oneself as the only doer is a mistake.
prasang.lesson: You are one cause among five; own your part, not the whole outcome.

verse.for_you: You are not the result of your work; success and failure come and go, while the one who acts stays whole through both.

verse.setting: Ribhu on the mark of the wise.

verse.line: Not pining for pleasures still to come, and enjoying the ones already here: that is wisdom.
verse.translation: Not longing for pleasures yet to come, and enjoying those that have come: this, unforced, is the mark of the wise.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥
verse.line: Do the work steadily, letting go of clinging. Stay the same in success and failure; that balance is yoga.
verse.translation: Established in yoga, do your work, Dhananjaya, giving up attachment, the same in success and failure. This evenness is called yoga.
verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.
verse.misuse: Even in success and failure doesn't mean indifferent to them; learn from both without being thrown.

prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.speaker: Seer
verse.setting: Follows the call to enjoy by letting go: how to live and work.
verse.sanskrit: कुर्वन्नेवेह कर्माणि जिजीविषेच्छतꣳ समाः । एवं त्वयि नान्यथेतोऽस्ति न कर्म लिप्यते नरे ॥
verse.line: Do your work and wish to live a full hundred years. Done in this spirit, action does not cling.
verse.translation: Doing your work here, you may wish to live a hundred years. For you there is no other way than this: done in this spirit, action does not cling to a person.
verse.why: Hold what you have lightly, keep working, and see yourself in everyone.

prasang.summary: Eighteen verses that open by saying everything belongs to the divine, so we should enjoy it without grasping. They go on to say we should work a full life without being bound, and see ourselves in all beings.
prasang.lesson: Hold what you have lightly, keep working, and see yourself in everyone.

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha teaches the disheartened young Rama that effort, not fate, shapes his life.
verse.sanskrit: यथा यथा प्रयत्नः स्याद्भवेदाशु फलं तथा । इति पौरुषमेवास्ति दैवमस्तु तदेव च ॥
verse.line: Results follow effort. Call it fate if you like, but it is the same effort.
verse.translation: As the effort, so quickly comes the fruit. So there is only effort; if you want to call it fate, it is that same effort.
verse.why: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

prasang.title: Vasishtha on self-effort: fate is only your past effort
prasang.summary: Vasishtha's first teaching to Rama is a long case for self-effort. What people call fate is simply the fruit of their own past effort, and present effort can overcome it, as the stronger of two rams wins. He also says not to torment yourself over what was beyond your power, and to steer your habits gently, like raising a child.
prasang.lesson: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

story.title: Hanuman's search and near despair
story.story_hook: Hanuman had searched every palace in Lanka by moonlight, and she was nowhere.
story.summary: Hanuman searches Lanka all night without finding Sita. He is close to despair, weighing what failure will mean for everyone, then tells himself that refusing to lose heart is the root of success, and searches again.
story.lesson: When you have looked everywhere, look again; giving up costs too much.

anchor.speaker: Hanuman
anchor.setting: Having searched all of Lanka without finding Sita, Hanuman fights off despair.
anchor.sanskrit: अनिर्वेदः श्रियो मूलमनिर्वेदः परं सुखम्। भूयस्तत्र विचेष्यामि न यत्र विचयः कृतः॥
anchor.line: Refusing to lose heart is the root of success. Look again where you have not yet looked.
anchor.translation: Not losing heart is the root of success; not losing heart is the highest happiness. I will search again, in the places I have not yet searched.
anchor.why: When you have looked everywhere, look again; giving up costs too much.
